newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Most Budapest grains prices limit-down.
newsitem.headline: Most Budapest grains prices limit-down.

text.p: Most grains futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) went down by the daily allowed limit on Monday due to good crop expectations, falling Chicago prices and uncertain export outlook, traders said.
Maturing July prices saw even more significant movements than the maximum allowed 400 forint limit per tonne as prices were freed up on the last day of trade.
"This was the moment of truth," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
July maize rose 760 forints to finish at 22,100 and despite 496 lots changing hands, 2,924 contracts remained to be delivered.
"Many (brokerages) chose to deliver at these high prices," Szolyka said.
Untraded October remained flat at 18,950 forints, November dropped 290 to 18,700 and all other maturities went limit-down ending at between 19,040 forints for December and 22,500 for July 1998.
Maturing milling wheat futures dropped 750 forints per tonne to 19,430 in moderate turnover, but only 440 lots remained to be delivered.
All other milling wheat maturities went limit-down to finish between 20,120 forints for August and 23,100 for May.
Maturing feed barley futures registered the sharpest fall with 1,310 forints ending at 17,800.
Szolyka said spot barley prices were also depressed due to a bumper crop expected.

"Spot barley prices are around 16,000 forints (per tonne) compared with 30,000 forints last year," he said, adding that last summer's high prices probably encouraged producers to plant more barley for this year.
All other barley maturities went limit-down and the May maturity opened at 21,600 forints.
Total grains turnover on the BCE rose to 1,273 lots or 583 million forints from Friday's 796 lots or 344 million forints.
Maize and milling wheat accounted for the bulk of turnover with 556 and 509 lots, respectively.
